If you have "and" in a commit message, it is probably 2 or more commits.

In this case you have 2 of 3 interfaces in the title and yet another one listed in the commit message body...
Done

Do you have a design document of what you're trying to accomplish.  This is about the 5th commit you've given with zero context, zero design, and just random words.  Please stop submitting random interfaces without any explaination.
I have updated the same in commit message as well https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76686

This is not clear - why do we need anything more than the "type" of the sensor which basically is in the path segment - such as sensor/temperature?

Can you explain the need for more description - what adds that, what uses it etc?

Also, why can't we use https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item.interface.yaml#L10?
Acknowledged
Why do we have a random string?
removed as suggested earlier in the commit from Deepak
Acknowledged
As commented elsewhere, this is the "what" part. How/Why is missing.
Done
Why does one have to add this to every interface/property when we have https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Time/EpochTime.interface.yaml?
Since the both properties are related and are defined for sensors hence kept in same interface.
Done

The "relation" can exist on the D-Bus object. A lot of properties might have associated timestamps - this doesn't mean we add that to all those interfaces. I recommend using an existing interface for timestamp.
Unresolving this

As per current design https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/architecture/sensor-architecture.md

Sensor object path can choose to implement other interfaces as well. If we define timestamp through other PDI it becomes difficult to associate it with Sensor.Value specifically and hence the reason its included in the same interface
Can you elaborate why? The object implementing Sensor.Value can also implement the timestamp/epoch interface.
Provided reply on similar comment above. Please check

For the use case where a timestamp is needed for both sensor value and sensor peak value, adding xyz.openbmc_project.Time.EpochTime interface can only provide timestamp for either sensor value or sensor peak value. What would be the approach for this case?

Aishwary is working on figuring how we solve the exact problem that you asked, but I recommended him to address that via a follow up commit. One approach I can think of is well defined segment names for <sensor>/<timestamp>
I will follow it up with a new patch
Not sure what the reference point is. This may need an example.
removed it from this commit
Acknowledged
Please say more here - something similar to https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78349
added more details

You need to add more detail - what other interfaces does the object implementing this need to also implement? The same things make me wonder (and I would recommend_ adding this as a property to Sensor.Value. The correlation becomes easier.
Acknowledged
Add default value? Also state if this is optional/mandatory and when is an implementation typically supposed to update this?
Added along with better description.
Acknowledged
Why is this readonly?
only server should be able to update the value and client should not be able to modify it. Hence made it read only
Hope this clarifiesthe reason to make it read only ?
Acknowledged
As I've been commenting elsewhere - we don't want to add this property here as it the interface for it exists already.

As per current design https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/architecture/sensor-architecture.md

Sensor object path can choose to implement other interfaces as well. If we define timestamp through other PDI it becomes difficult to associate it with Sensor.Value specifically and hence the reason its included in the same interface
Can you elaborate why? The object implementing Sensor.Value can also implement the timestamp/epoch interface.

Sensor Object apart from xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value can additionally implement these interfaces

xyz.openbmc_project.Control.FanSpeed
xyz.openbmc_project.Control.FanPwm
xyz.openbmc_project.State.Decorator.OperationalStatus
xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.*

Additing xyz.openbmc_project.Time.EpochTime to sensor object would make "Elapsed" property ambigous, could be misleading and I think it can be interpretted in many ways for eg the Elapsed time since last sensor value last updated by service hosting the sensor. IMO the generic nature of the Elapsed interface makes it not ideal unless its meaning become more specific for sensors.

It doesn't have to be ambiguous. You can document the expected behavior in this YAML (see my proposed D-Bus guielines where I've given examples where such companion interfaces are clearly documented). I think the most common use of it would be to understand when the sensor was refreshed.
Thanks for guidelines. Please check i have updated as per the recommendation.
Acknowledged
Did you want to update Sensor.Value ot Metric.Value? Please resolve comments once you think you've addressed them.
Really sorry for the goof up. It has been fixed now.
Acknowledged
addressed all review comments
Addressed all review comments
When you say "max value" here, do you mean the property on line 28? If yes, then use the term MaxValue. If this is something else, then it isn't clear to me.
@deepak.kodihalli.83@gmail.com please review.
This is not a great commit title.  Extended it for what purpose?
Updated commit message

This is not a workable proposal.

1. We should not add a new property like this for all sensors when it is only relevant to specific implementations (which are rare).
2. There is no way to communicate if this feature is supported.
3. Some day someone may want to add a "TroughValue" and then you'll have no idea if the timestamp is for the Peak or the Trough.

Maintaining a peak value does not seem appropriate for an individual sensor.  Isn't this a telemetry item?  Or is it a separate "sensor"?  It seems like there are lots of potential telemetry you might want to capture on a sensor: peak, trough, average [over a period of time], etc.  I do not think we should handle this by adding properties to a sensor one at a time.

Thanks @patrick@stwcx.xyz for re-review on this one, the PeakValue is captured in the design doc here(Max Observed Power)
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76686/20/designs/nvidia-gpu.md#57

To address your concerns
#1 -> I think its a good idea to separate it out to a new interface(PeakValue.interface)

#2 -> Implementing the interface would be optional and an indiciation whether the feature is supported or not

#3 -> adding a separate interface should address this issue as well. Each specific metric can have its own interface and related properties like you mentioned for average, trough etc..
Done
I see no reference to "Peak" in this design document.  I have no idea how this is relevant.
Please refer "Max Observed Power"  here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76686/20/designs/nvidia-gpu.md#57

CC: @patrick@stwcx.xyz
Acknowledged
This should also be readonly?
Acknowledged

I think we need some discussion on why this is different from telemetry and why we should go this direction.

I'm a little concerned in a few aspects:

1. We already have telemetry, which is hardly used.
2. There seems to only be one design that is going to take advantage of this, which hasn't reached consensus yet.  I don't know how this is going to be used by Redfish since it is not a "normal" sensor.
3. We already had a poor situation with thresholds where we ended up having to create N optional separate interfaces to track them, and we solved this differently with metric thresholds (to reduce the sprawl of optional interfaces).  We might want to go that route here also?

(Regarding #3, the hope is that someone refactors sensor thresholds to use the metric threshold design at some point also.)

To address the concern #1 and #3 have added a common interface to track the various limits for specific sensor or metric. It should make the same interface extensible with various new limits if one wants to add, for eg you pointed out trough value earlier can be done by extending the enum.

For #2, Sensor schema already defines PeakReading and PeakReadingTime property 
https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Sensor.v1_10_1.yaml

Hope this addresses the concerns.

Thanks,
Aishwary
Done
@patrick@stwcx.xyz changes are done that should address the concerns listed above, can you please take a look?

How had the concerns been addressed?  All I see is yet another _new_ interface that still isn't related to anything in any design document.

> I think we need some discussion on why this is different from telemetry and why we should go this direction.


My very first statement was this. ^

Design doc here already covers "Maximum observered power" 
 under Power Management https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76686/21/designs/nvidia-gpu.md

Please note that the Maximum Observed Power is being reported by the device itself and bmc is not computing it based on sensor values sampled by the bmc service

Also like to add that I have also looked at the telemetry design  
https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/telemetry.md
and the xyz/openbmc_project/Telemetry/Report.interface.yaml interface may offer similar stats but key difference is that the BMC is sampling the telemetry and interface definition is tied to RF metric report model, while in this case the max observed power is being reported by the device itself.

This needs rephrasing. This is not about a device but about sensors and metrics. Look at https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Common/Threshold.interface.yaml.
Acknowledged
I would call the interface Statistics (as it could include Average as well) and this property as Value.
Updated the interface name and property name, please re-review
